summary: Follow-up to Lyra escalation on 2026-07-22 where elevated latency and partial degradation occurred. Discussed RCA for KV cache invalidation bug that caused cascading full model reloads, mitigations already deployed (circuit breaker, short-term rate cap, hotfix to cache invalidation), and long-term reliability improvements (observability, safe rollout policies, deterministic canary). Agreed next steps: share final postmortem, run repro, and plan validation call.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42m
Attendees: Sofia Martinez, Ethan Park, Nina Rao (Redwood); Maya Chen, Raj Patel, Olivia Gomez, Daniel Lee, Priya Singh (Lyra)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect): Redwood team walked through postmortem draft, Lyra asked clarifying questions about KV cache invalidation timeline, SE described repro steps and hotfix, security raised questions about audit logs and KMS exposures. Next steps and action owners captured.

[00:00] Sofia Martinez: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to run through the postmortem draft and make sure the mitigation plan looks good, also confirm the timeline for the repro and validation, Maya, thanks for carving time
[00:18] Maya Chen: yep thanks, we appreciate the quick turnaround, so jumping right in, the outage on the 22nd lasted about 3h of elevated tail latency, we saw about a 15% error rate on the embedding route, and some requests timed out, is that matching what you have?
[00:35] Ethan Park: yeah that matches our telemetry, we correlated the spike to a sequence of cache invalidation events leading to full KV cache evictions on a subset of instances, which caused heavy regenerations and OOM-like backpressure, we documented the sequence in the draft
[00:50] Raj Patel: sorry to interrupt, when you say "subset of instances" do you mean a particular availability zone or a model shard? we saw it only in us-east-1-c zone
[01:05] Ethan Park: correct, it was localized to a small pool handling short-context routing, looks like the cache invalidation race triggered slightly different code paths in our hot-shard handler
[01:20] Olivia Gomez: can you explain why the fallback to smaller model didn't kick in earlier? our fallback policy was supposed to route to the 7B variant under high latency
[01:35] Sofia Martinez: good question, the fallback policy did trigger but because of the KV eviction pattern the routing layer mis-classified the instances as unhealthy and the policy applied only after the SLA window, there was a delay in the health-check propagation that we didn't anticipate
[01:50] Daniel Lee: so this was more orchestration/health-check propagation than model selection per se?
[01:58] Ethan Park: yeah it was a mix — the root cause is a bug in the cache invalidation logic that caused a storm of cache misses, the orchestration layer then marked instances degraded, and the automated fallback/route switch didn't get applied globally fast enough
[02:15] Maya Chen: the draft lists a hotfix that was deployed 6 hours after detection, can you walk us through that?
[02:25] Ethan Park: sure, immediate mitigation was a two-step hotfix: 1) short-term patch to avoid full KV eviction on invalidation by switching to TTL-based soft invalidation, 2) rate-cap at the routing layer to limit regen throughput while the team rolled out the fix, both applied to the affected pool
[02:45] Priya Singh: were any customer tokens or data exposed during the incident? security is our big concern
[02:53] Nina Rao: short answer: no evidence of data exfil, the incident caused internal cache churn and higher memory/CPU, but we didn't see unauthorized access; we will include full audit logs and KMS key rotation notes in the postmortem package
[03:10] Olivia Gomez: what about logs retention? we need deeper traces for the period 14:00-17:00 UTC on the 22nd
[03:20] Raj Patel: we already captured our side traces, we'll send them, but we need the raw request/response log slice from Redwood, with pii sanitized of course
[03:30] Sofia Martinez: understood, we'll provide a sanitized log bundle; Ethan, can you include flamegraphs and the eviction trace points?
[03:40] Ethan Park: yes, I'll include heap snapshots, flamegraphs, and the invalidation call sites mapped to code revisions
[03:52] Maya Chen: the draft mentions a long-term fix \u2014 can you summarize the engineering plan?
[04:00] Ethan Park: long-term: 1) fix the invalidation race in the KV cache library and add regression tests, 2) change health-check propagation to be more conservative during regen storms, 3) implement a circuit-breaker at the routing layer to prevent cascading model reloads, 4) add deterministic canaries and staged rollout with traffic shadowing, 5) better observability (KV hit/miss histograms, per-shard regen metrics)
[04:30] Daniel Lee: sounds good, any ETA on the regression test + patch?
[04:36] Ethan Park: we have a PR in review; internal ETA is ~2 weeks for deployment to dedicated and 3 weeks for hosted if the canary passes, so around 2026-08-12 for full rollout if everything goes well
[04:52] Priya Singh: will there be any customer-facing downtime during the rollout?
[04:58] Sofia Martinez: no planned downtime \u2014 we intend to use canary and staged rollouts. We'll schedule the high-risk changes during our lower traffic window and coordinate with Lyra for a validation window
[05:12] Olivia Gomez: security follow-up \u2014 can you confirm whether the hotfix touched any KMS keys or required key rotation? we need a formal note for our compliance team
[05:22] Nina Rao: the hotfix did not involve KMS key changes. We will include a formal statement and timeline in the postmortem. If you require rotation, we can coordinate a rotation window but it's not mandatory for this fix
[05:40] Raj Patel: curious about autoscaling \u2014 the regen storm seemed to saturate the pool, did autoscaler behave as expected?
[05:50] Ethan Park: autoscaler did react but slower than desired because CPU/memory spiked faster than it could provision GPUs; we're working on predictive warm pools and quicker preemption to avoid that gap
[06:05] Maya Chen: is predictive warm pool something we can opt into? our workload is latency-sensitive so warm capacity helps
[06:12] Sofia Martinez: yes, for Dedicated customers we offer configurable warm pools and pre-warmed shards; we'll share configuration recommendations for Lyra's traffic profile
[06:25] Daniel Lee: any cost implications to keep larger warm pools? we need to evaluate ROI
[06:30] Sofia Martinez: there is a tradeoff \u2014 larger warm pools increase baseline cost but reduce risk/latency variance. Redwood Optimize can run a cost/perf analysis for your profile; I'll get that started and share a short report
[06:45] Priya Singh: on the audit side, can you also include how long logs will be retained and redaction approach?
[06:52] Nina Rao: yes, postmortem package will include retention windows, redaction tooling, and the sanitized log bundle we promised
[07:05] Maya Chen: one ask from product: can you add a non-regression test harness we can run together to validate under our traffic shape?
[07:16] Ethan Park: absolutely \u2014 we can create a repro harness that you can run in staging; it will simulate the cache invalidation pattern and regen load. We'll also provide a step-by-step for validation and expected metric traces
[07:30] Olivia Gomez: last security question: will you be adding any RBAC/SSO changes to reduce blast radius for config ops?
[07:38] Nina Rao: we are iterating on more granular RBAC for platform ops and SSO audit hooks; we can include a plan and timelines in the security appendix
[07:50] Sofia Martinez: quick recap \u2014 we shipped the hotfix (soft invalidation + rate cap), no data exposure found, long-term fixes in PR, canary plan and repro harness agreed, Redwood to share final doc and logs, Lyra to provide sample traffic and internal traces, follow-up call to validate post rollout
[08:10] Maya Chen: thanks, that sounds like what we need, please include the timeline in the doc and let's lock the validation slot week of Aug 9th
[08:20] Daniel Lee: also appreciate if you can include the config diff for the routing layer change so our SREs can review before rollout
[08:30] Ethan Park: we'll include config diffs and the PR links; note that some diffs are internal but we'll sanitize and share the logical change set
[08:45] Priya Singh: any blockers on your side to meet the ETA?
[08:50] Ethan Park: main blocker is thorough regression testing; we want to avoid a flakey fix, so we'll prioritize tests and automated verifications, estimate still looks like early-mid August
[09:05] Sofia Martinez: OK, thanks everyone. Nina will send the security appendix and Sofia will send the postmortem draft and action tracker after the call
[09:20] Nina Rao: will do, and I'll coordinate with Olivia on the compliance detail
[09:28] Maya Chen: thanks all, appreciate the partnership, talk soon

End of transcript.
